rationale: Bcheck deliberately stops tracking a local whose address is passed; the audited value remains reachable through the operation's protected input, output, receipt, or indexed graph-root carrier.

The reported child or capsule is borrowed from a directly protected argument or from an attribute, protected slot, closure, environment binding, or transaction value whose owner remains rooted across the audited call.

The function uses reviewed branch-dependent or variable-count protection accounting that bcheck cannot model; every branch has an exact balance, any address-taken graph output has an indexed protected carrier, and maacheck plus the dynamic memory gates cover stack discipline.

The reported value and every borrowed child are retained by a direct PROTECT or an explicitly protected vector, environment, transaction chain, or indexed root carrier before the subsequent allocating operation.
The test-only ALTREP callback deliberately uses caller-balanced protection to create an adversarial collection schedule; it is not shipped production behavior.
